item.title: Why Greenland Could Spur Europe’s Digital Awakening
item.description: U.S. pressure over Greenland is pushing Europe to confront a deeper vulnerability: its dependence on U.S. tech. The result could be a profound shift in cloud, AI, and digital sovereignty across the European Union.

item.title: Trump’s Greenland Ambition Is About U.S. Power, Not Alliances
item.description: Trump's push for Greenland isn't about NATO security—it's about controlling vast sums in rare earth minerals. European appeals to Cold War alliances miss the point of his America First doctrine, which prioritizes U.S. economic gain above all else.

item.title: Japan Poised for Early General Election
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s plan to dissolve the lower house of the Japanese parliament could give her party a mandate for strong leadership—or it could exacerbate current governance challenges.

item.title: China’s Rare Earth Campaign Against Japan
item.description: China’s imposition of new rare earth export restrictions on Japan, following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s remarks on Taiwan, represents an escalation in China–Japan tensions and highlights Beijing’s increasing reliance on mineral export controls as a deterrence tool.

item.title: Securing the Future of the U.S. Biopharmaceutical Industry: The Most-Favored-Nation Paradox
item.description: The administration’s success in securing massive investment pledges from the industry to reshore manufacturing needs to be reinforced. Its positive impact will be undermined if the long-term consequence of its most-favored-nation pricing policy weakens the foundations of U.S. innovation.

item.title: Leveraging Japan’s Appetite for U.S. Investment and Partnership in Pharmaceuticals and Biotechnology
item.description: The United States and Japan can strengthen their economic security and competitiveness by taking advantage of shared interests and new opportunities in the pharmaceuticals and biotechnology industries.

item.title: Would Air Strikes Against Iran Work?
item.description: History shows that air strikes alone struggle to achieve complex policy goals, but used in Iran now, they could trigger a domino effect that leads to the collapse of Iran's repressive authoritarian regime.
